scope: cold-process repeatability and controlled CPU-contention audit of the frozen optimized pi0.5-to-Panda CPU replay
research_question: Does the v0.2.0 optimized atomic assurance result remain reproducible across independent cold processes, and how does bounded CPU contention change the observed latency and publication outcomes?

input_contract.source_rows: the 90 direct-dispatch rows crossed with three registered Panda scenes

conditions.load_model: four independent deterministic Python busy-loop workers started before each replay and terminated after it

replicates.case_reset: delegated to the v0.2.0 optimized replay protocol
replicates.process_reset: one fresh Python process per trial
replicates.randomness: PYTHONHASHSEED=0; frozen source artifact and fixed protocol; no policy inference

recorded_outcomes: per-profile execute, hold, and constraint-safe candidate counts
P50, P95, maximum supervisor and worker latency
wall-clock duration, child return code, and timeout state
condition-level mean, standard deviation, min, and max

interpretation.repeatability: descriptive only; three replicates are an engineering stability signal, not an inferential sample
interpretation.cpu_load: diagnostic host-contention stress and not a hardware certification
claim_boundary: Frozen official responses are replayed; the pi0.5 checkpoint is not executed.
LIBERO actions are cross-controller Panda inputs, not native Panda policy outputs.
Independent cases do not provide closed-loop policy feedback or task success.
Python CPU timing is best effort and is not a hard-real-time guarantee.
MuJoCo geometry and inverse dynamics are not physical-robot safety certification.
A repeatability audit cannot establish robot-level safety or generalization.
